## Body

# Generated notice inventories need two kinds of closure

A runtime inventory can share its blind spot with its tests. In #194, the enum declared a kind separately from ALL, while reservation and every-kind tests enumerated only ALL. A new typed producer could therefore exist without reservation and still pass. The repair generates enum, ALL and prefix matching from one notice_kinds! declaration. A second-origin test reads that declaration from source and compares names, order and prefix bytes with compiled ALL. Deliberately dropping a compiled entry killed this check while the ordinary refusal test stayed green.

An exhaustive table does not prove exhaustive producer coverage. The shipped background sidecar passed hand-built bg- completion/cancellation IDs directly to enqueue_turn; a scanner limited to msg_id assignments and *_id helpers missed it. Trace every reachable producer into the queue. Include ID-bearing call arguments, discovered from msg_id/dedupe_key parameters, alongside assignments and helper returns. Test a new unregistered literal through a real helper call, not only an already-listed prefix.

Keep the proof boundary explicit: this scanner recognizes construction shapes, not complete Rust data flow. Ordinary shim-generated IDs are a different namespace/scope. Preserve existing prefix and suffix bytes when centralizing a mint, and separately document any intentional re-keying and upgrade replay behavior.

Evidence: #194 repair and retained omitted-ALL, sidecar-mint and new-helper-argument mutants; core notice_id and daemon notice_ids tests.
